literal_source_claim: The compatibility of the union of theories.
canonical_claim_candidate: For first-order theories T1 and T2 in languages L1 and L2, if there is no sentence phi in the common language L1 intersection L2 such that T1 entails phi and T2 entails not phi, then T1 union T2 is satisfiable (with consistency/satisfiability and language-translation conventions fixed by the selected source).
domain_and_universes: Provisionally two first-order languages with a specified common sublanguage and theories transported into a common union language; exact universe levels, language morphisms, and theory transports are open.
quantifiers: first-order languages L0, L1, and L2
specified embeddings of the common language L0 into L1 and L2
theories T1 over L1 and T2 over L2
sentences phi over L0 for the separation condition
hypotheses: provisional: no common-language sentence is entailed by T1 while its negation is entailed by T2
all language translations and the common union language preserve sentence semantics
conclusion: Provisional: the translations of T1 and T2 into their common union language have a jointly satisfiable union.

alternate_encodings.target: a Robinson joint consistency formulation using syntactic consistency and derivability
alternate_encodings.relationship: intended equivalent only after soundness/completeness and language-transport bridges

alternate_encodings.target: the same-language claim that consistency of T1 and T2 separately implies consistency of T1 union T2
alternate_encodings.relationship: not equivalent and false in general

excluded_degenerate_cases: Theories with incompatible common-language consequences are not asserted jointly consistent. Empty theories and empty nonlogical signatures should remain included once a source convention is fixed. No countability, completeness, or disjoint-signature assumption may be silently added.
